key_insight: A cycle-consistent neural surrogate can both predict tokamak edge plasma fields quickly and infer the underlying control inputs with high reliability.
engineering_relevance: This enables near-real-time analysis, parameter scans, uncertainty-aware decision support, and potential digital-twin or control applications for tokamak edge and divertor operation.
method: Conditional U-Net forward model maps five control parameters to 2D SOLPS-ITER plasma fields.
Optimization-based inverse model is built on the frozen forward network and trained with cycle-consistency.
Ensemble MLPs predict midplane and divertor profiles with uncertainty estimates.
evidence_signal: The forward model reports normalized RMSE below 2.6% and Pearson correlations above 0.95, while cycle-consistency raises average cyclical R^2 from 0.59 to 0.99 and recovers all five control parameters with Pearson r >= 0.97.
watch_item: Performance depends on the training database and warm-start strategy, so extrapolation to unseen regimes or poorly covered operating points may remain risky.
paper_title: Cycle-Consistent and Uncertainty-Aware Neural Surrogates for Tokamak Edge Plasmas
